expected_level_description: You can: - manage the monthly reporting cycle for a directorate or programme - build cost models, such as the full cost of a digital service or the unit cost of a transaction - analyse spending trends and advise managers on actions to stay within budget - challenge budget holders constructively on their forecasts

You can: - lead budget setting and forecasting for a directorate or large programme - model scenarios and sensitivities, such as inflation, delays, or changes in funding - build multi-year forecasts for digital programmes, including the running costs that follow investment - present forecasts and risks to senior managers

You can: - lead the financial case for complex digital investments, such as a new clinical system or a move to cloud - appraise options using net present value, sensitivity analysis, and risk adjustment - check that benefits are realistic, measurable, and owned - track spending and benefits after approval

You can: - advise managers on funding rules, including ring-fenced and time-limited funding - manage capital and revenue limits for a programme or directorate - prepare returns and evidence for funders and spending controls

skill: Financial management for digital, data and technology
expected_level_description: *Senior leadership skill: the UK GDaD PCF defines it with one statement, not by level.* You can: - own, manage and optimise budgets across digital, data and technology - secure appropriate investment to deliver organisational strategy and priorities - negotiate investments in shared technologies across the organisation and across government Examples of leadership using this skill: - prioritising competing demands for investment in people, infrastructure and innovation across digital, data and technology to maximise value - identifying risk to critical services and influencing stakeholders to increase investment to ensure they are maintained - balancing short-term tactical gains with longer-term strategies to ensure value now and in the future

You can: - estimate the value of each item on your roadmap - compare effort to value when deciding priorities - decide when it's appropriate to reuse something, and when it's not - decide how and when to escalate risk in achieving value - discuss estimates with stakeholders to validate understanding - analyse the benefit of investment against anticipated outcomes

You can: - work with the team to develop and maintain an understanding of stakeholders - work with the team to develop and implement stakeholder communications strategies - identify and resolve issues, influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively - build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders
You can: - supervise day-to-day work and give feedback - take part in recruitment and induction - hold regular one-to-one conversations

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
